question: Should ordinary conversation messages expire within an active session based on wall-clock TTL, or should TTL remain tool-result-only while compaction and session rotation manage conversation history?
rationale: Both directions are plausible, but they have materially different retention, memory, cost, compatibility, and authorization semantics that cannot be selected from current implementation alone.

options.title: Keep TTL tool-result-only
options.body: Clarify the documented contract and use compaction plus explicit session age or turn limits to bound normal conversation history.

options.title: Add explicit history retention
options.body: Introduce a separately named retention mode with defined summarization, persistence, authorization, migration, and recovery behavior rather than changing `cache-ttl` semantics.

recommendation.title: Keep TTL tool-result-only
recommendation.body: Clarify the documented contract and use compaction plus explicit session age or turn limits to bound normal conversation history.

likelyOwner.reason: The latest review already framed this product boundary and history connects this person to the current session lifecycle behavior.
